newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco, Daewoo work on detailed accord.
newsitem.headline: Morocco, Daewoo work on detailed accord.

text.p: Morocco and South Korean giant Daewoo Corporation are working out final details of a $500 million investment in Moroccan telecommunications, tourism and electronics signed in July.

Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj told Reuters on Wednesday: "Daewoo officials are serious...We are working together to implement the agreement details soon...It is a positive thing for both Morocco and Daewoo company."
Daewoo President Woo-Choong Kim and Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali signed the accord in Rabat and King Hassan received the Daewoo president on July 23.
The finance ministry said in a report: "Daewoo is deeply engaged in Morocco, it will invest $500 million of which $220 million will be devoted to telecommunications."
"Daewoo will be associated with an international operator in the expected tender for the GSM mobile telephone network," it said.
Kabbaj said the government expected a bill on GSM to be approved during the autumn session starting on October 11.
Moroccan telecommunications are under the control of the state-owned Office National des Postes et telecommunications.
The investment will also create 3,000 jobs in Morocco.
The deals also cover a $100 million investment "to renovate and extend" the Rabat Hyatt Regency hotel, the ministry said.
The remaining amount will be invested in the Nouaceur Technopole industrial area, close to Morocco's main airport at Casablanca.
"A Daewoo plant of household appliances and television sets will be established in the Technopole zone...Most of the plant output will destined for exports," it said.
Earlier this month, Trade Minister Driss Jettou visited Daewoo's electronics plants in Poland. He also plans a working meeting with Daewoo officials in London at end September, officials said.
Morocco faces tough competition from other North African countries, including Tunisia, campaigning to attract foreign investors such as Daewoo.
